subject: Litigation hold: preservation & on-demand snapshot procedure
messages:
From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@aurorafinance.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: audit-request@aurorafinance.com
Date: 2025-11-29T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Request: litigation hold process + sample artifacts

Jonas,

We need to stand up a litigation hold for a pending regulatory inquiry and require details on how Redwood preserves audit logs and can produce point-in-time snapshots on demand. Specifically, could you confirm: 

- Retention immutability: can you produce an immutable snapshot of audit logs for a given time window (UTC-based) and provide tamper-evidence (hashes/signatures)?
- Snapshot delivery: formats supported, max file size, and typical delivery timeline for a 90-day slice (approx 30M log events).
- Chain of custody: what artifacts do you provide (manifest, checksums, access logs, personnel who exported)?
- Redaction options: can you redact PII at export time and provide a redaction log?

We will need a sample manifest and a template chain-of-custody for our legal team to review. Can you respond with the ops procedure and an SLA for delivery?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Rogers
Senior Counsel, Litigation Response
Aurora Finance

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-29T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: litigation hold process + sample artifacts

Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attach a short manifest and a chain-of-custody template for your review (see attachments). We can provide a formal runbook if Aurora wants a signed appendix in an agreement.

Summary answers:
- Retention immutability: we support point-in-time immutable snapshots for audit logs. Snapshots are computed from the append-only audit ledger, signed with a service-level HMAC and stored with SHA-256 checksums. Each snapshot includes a manifest with per-file hashes and a snapshot-level signature.
- Snapshot delivery: we export NDJSON or Parquet bundles, compressed (.ndjson.gz / .parquet.gz). For a 90-day slice at ~30M events we typically produce a multi-part archive (sharded by time) and deliver via pre-signed S3 URLs or encrypted transfer to your SFTP endpoint. Typical timeline: 48–72 hours after request for standard priority; expedited 24 hours available as add-on.
- Chain of custody: delivered artifacts include manifest.pdf (human-readable), manifest.json (machine-readable), per-file checksums, export audit (who initiated, job IDs, server IDs, AWS region, timestamps), and the signed snapshot token. We also include a CSV export of the operator actions and IP addresses.
- Redaction: we support export-time redaction profiles (pattern-based and field-level). Redaction is applied to exported files; a redaction log is generated that lists original field identifiers, redaction rule id, and replacement marker. Note: redaction is deterministic and irreversible once applied to an export; we keep the unredacted ledger under the original retention rules unless a legal hold instructs otherwise.

Attachments: snapshot_manifest_v1.pdf (example), chain_of_custody_template.xlsx (template).

Next steps:
1) Confirm desired time window and delivery method.
2) If you want tamper-evident notarization, we can route the snapshot signature to an external timestamping authority (extra cost).
3) For litigation holds longer than 12 months we recommend a reserved evidence-retention contract to guarantee retention tiers and storage pricing.

I'll loop in Marissa for SLA/coordination and Laura for legal ops acceptance.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: litigation hold process + sample artifacts

Emily —

Quick clarifications from Legal Ops side: 

- Preservation scope: please confirm whether Aurora requires preservation of request/response payloads (application layer content) in addition to platform audit logs. Our snapshot covers platform-generated audit logs; application payloads are preserved per your account/data logs settings or via an integration we can enable.
- Access controls: snapshots are delivered encrypted; we can require a customer-managed KMS key for encrypting delivery archives.
- Export redaction certification: we can provide a signed statement of redaction steps taken (rule ids, operator id), but we cannot certify the absence of PII beyond the redaction rules you approve.

If you can confirm the above, we'll schedule the export and provide a formal SOW with timelines and pricing.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Legal
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Emily — technical follow-up from engineering: 

Couple of implementation details you may find useful for scope planning and the SOW: 

- Sharding and indexes: exports are sharded hourly for large windows; each shard contains an index file (index.ndjson) with byte offsets so you can stream-validate without decompressing the whole archive.
- Checksums and notarization: per-file SHA-256 is in the manifest; we can also provide a Merkle root across shard checksums if you require an additional layer of tamper proofing for cryptographic verification.
- Filtering and selectors: export jobs accept selectors (time range, event type, tenant id, request id). We recommend a pre-run validation where Aurora provides a sample query to validate expected cardinality.
- Performance and throttling: standard export workers run at a controlled I/O ceiling; we can enable burst workers for expedited dumps. Cost and IO limits will be in the SOW.

Operational notes: we will:
1) Create a hold ticket, tag your account, and pin the retention policy to "litigation-hold" which suspends normal deletion.
2) Run a dry-run export (metadata-only) for Aurora to validate manifests.
3) After sign-off, run the full export and deliver via your chosen channel.

If that looks good we can set a delivery SLA of 48 hours for the dry-run and 72 hours for the full export on standard priority. Expedited delivery (24 hours) is possible with approval.

-Karthik
